app-server-events.title: model/verification notification parsed from stream but never emitted

context-compaction.title: isModelGenerated excludes .contextCompaction, contradicting upstream is_model_generated_item (ContextCompaction => true)
context-compaction.rustEvidence: core/src/context_manager/history.rs:681-699 is_model_generated_item explicitly returns true for both `ResponseItem::Compaction { .. } | ResponseItem::ContextCompaction { .. } => true`. This boundary feeds items_after_last_model_generated_item (history.rs:298-305) which feeds get_total_token_usage (history.rs:309-327) — the value compared against auto_compact_limit in session/turn.rs:480 and :749.
context-compaction.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/ContextManager.swift:71-77 isModelGenerated returns true only for `.agentMessage, .reasoning`; it lists `.contextCompaction` (and `.commandExecution`) in the `return false` arm. ContextManager.swift:106-111 itemsAfterLastModelGenerated() uses this boundary; ContextManager.swift:132-136 totalTokenUsage() sums estimateItemTokens over items after that boundary.
context-compaction.description: Upstream treats a ContextCompaction item as a model-generated boundary, so after a remote compaction (whose installed history ends with a .contextCompaction marker — see SessionEngine.swift:2092 appending `.contextCompaction`), items_after_last_model_generated is empty and totalTokenUsage == last server total. The Swift port does NOT treat .contextCompaction as a boundary, so itemsAfterLastModelGenerated walks back past the marker to the last .agentMessage/.reasoning (or returns empty only if none exist), causing the synthesized post-compaction user/summary messages to be re-counted on top of the re-baselined lastServerTotalTokens. This can overstate context usage and trigger the next auto-compact earlier than upstream. (The recomputeTokenUsage() re-baseline at SessionEngine.swift:2161 partially masks this but does not make the boundary semantics match.)
context-compaction.fixRecommendation: In Sources/HarnessCore/ContextManager.swift:71-77, move `.contextCompaction` out of the false arm into the true arm so isModelGenerated returns true for it, matching upstream `ContextCompaction => true`.

context-compaction.title: isModelGenerated treats tool-call items (.commandExecution) as non-model-generated, unlike upstream FunctionCall boundary
context-compaction.rustEvidence: core/src/context_manager/history.rs:681-699: is_model_generated_item returns true for FunctionCall, ToolSearchCall, WebSearchCall, ImageGenerationCall, CustomToolCall, LocalShellCall (the model-emitted call side), while FunctionCallOutput/ToolSearchOutput/CustomToolCallOutput return false. The last model-emitted CALL is the boundary; its OUTPUT(s) recorded after it are counted as 'items after'.
context-compaction.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/ContextManager.swift:71-77 places `.commandExecution` in the `return false` arm. The Swift ThreadItem model unifies a call and its output into a single .commandExecution item, so there is no separate call-side boundary item.
context-compaction.description: Because Swift collapses call+output into one .commandExecution and treats it as non-model-generated, the items_after boundary for a turn ending in tool calls lands at the last .agentMessage/.reasoning rather than at the trailing function CALL as upstream does. The set of items counted as 'after the boundary' therefore differs (Swift counts the whole commandExecution; upstream counts only the output portion after the call). Practical impact on totalTokenUsage is bounded since both count trailing tool output, but the boundary semantics diverge and can shift the auto-compact trigger point for tool-heavy turns. This is a consequence of the unified-item model; documented here for completeness.
context-compaction.fixRecommendation: Either treat .commandExecution as model-generated in ContextManager.swift:71-77 (closer to upstream's FunctionCall=true) and account for the unified call+output cost accordingly, or document this as an accepted consequence of the unified ThreadItem model. Lower priority than the .contextCompaction fix.

tools-router.title: tool_search discovery path is never wired; model cannot discover deferred tools
tools-router.rustEvidence: core/src/tools/handlers/tool_search.rs + tool_search_spec.rs register a model-visible tool_search (gated on Feature::ToolSearch, default_enabled()==true per features/src/tests.rs:193, plus model_info.supports_search_tool); router.rs:93-110 routes the model's ToolSearchCall and activates matched deferred tools.

tools-router.description: Upstream exposes tool_search by default so the model can discover deferred (lazily-loaded) tools at runtime. In the Swift port the tool_search tool is never installed (dead code), so the model has no way to discover or activate any deferred tool; the only deferred tool (workflow) is reachable solely through the host-side /workflow trigger. This is a behavioral gap beyond the already-documented wire-envelope divergence (ToolRouter.swift:421-446).
tools-router.fixRecommendation: Either call `router.installToolSearch()` during DefaultTools.register (accepting the documented function-only wire shape) so deferred tools become model-discoverable, or remove the dead installToolSearch/performToolSearch/BM25 code if discovery is intentionally host-driven only. Document the chosen path next to the existing finding-4 note.

tools-router.title: FunctionCallError::Fatal (turn-aborting) collapsed into an ordinary failed ToolResult
tools-router.rustEvidence: core/src/tools/parallel.rs:70 maps `FunctionCallError::Fatal(message)` to `Err(CodexErr::Fatal(message))` which aborts the whole turn; registry.rs:391 returns Fatal for an incompatible payload and :525 for 'tool produced no output'. Non-fatal RespondToModel errors become a failed function_call_output (parallel.rs:71,158-165).
tools-router.swiftStatus: Sources/Tools/ToolRouter.swift:212-264 dispatch() turns every thrown error into a failed ToolResult (success:false) with the message as output; there is no Fatal path that aborts the turn. dispatchNestedFromCode similarly returns a string.
tools-router.description: Upstream distinguishes fatal tool errors (which terminate the turn with CodexErr::Fatal) from model-recoverable errors (returned to the model as a failed output). The Swift router has no Fatal concept: all tool failures are surfaced as a recoverable failed result, so an upstream-fatal condition (e.g. incompatible payload kind) would instead be fed back to the model rather than aborting the turn. Low impact in normal operation since these conditions are rare.
tools-router.fixRecommendation: Introduce a fatal error channel from dispatch() (e.g. a ToolError subtype or a thrown error the SessionEngine treats as turn-fatal) for the upstream Fatal cases, so the turn aborts rather than returning a recoverable failed output.

config.title: Project-local config layers are applied without trust gating (upstream disables untrusted project layers)
config.rustEvidence: config/src/loader/mod.rs:1162-1225 — load_project_layers calls trust_context.decision_for_dir(&dir) and disabled_reason_for_decision; non-trusted dirs get a disabled_reason and the layer is built via ConfigLayerEntry::new_disabled (mod.rs:869-872). disabled_reason_for_decision (mod.rs:828-844) returns Some(...) for any dir that is not explicitly Trusted (Untrusted OR unknown). state.rs:497-510 get_layers filters `!layer.is_disabled()`, so effective_config()/origins() EXCLUDE disabled project layers. The disabled_reason is also surfaced on ConfigLayer (v2/config.rs:298-304).
config.swiftStatus: Sources/Config/Config.swift:868-963 loadProjectLocalLayers loads every discovered .codex/config.toml unconditionally and appends it as an active layer (line 959). There is no trust_level lookup, no disabled_reason, and no concept of a disabled layer anywhere in Sources/Config/ (grep for trust/Untrusted/disabledReason returns only doc-comment mentions about admin-trusted system layers). RequestRouter config/read layer emission (RequestRouter.swift:1964-1982) never sets disabledReason.
config.description: Upstream only honors a project-local .codex/config.toml when the directory (or its project/repo root) is explicitly marked Trusted in the user's [projects] trust map; otherwise the layer is loaded but DISABLED and contributes nothing to the effective config (and is reported with a disabledReason in config/read layers). Swift applies ALL project-local configs regardless of trust, so a cloned/untrusted repo's .codex/config.toml takes effect in the Swift port even though upstream ignores it. This is a behavioral and security divergence and also a config/read wire gap (missing disabledReason).
config.fixRecommendation: In Sources/Config/Config.swift, thread the merged [projects.<key>].trust_level map into loadProjectLocalLayers; for each project dir compute a trust decision against the normalized dir/project-root/repo-root keys (mirror decision_for_dir), and when the decision is not Trusted, mark the layer disabled (add a `disabledReason: String?` to ConfigLayer and exclude disabled layers from merged/resolved/leafOrigins composition in Config.init). Surface disabledReason in RequestRouter.swift config/read layers[] output.

config.title: config write keyPath parsing diverges: Swift adds quoting/escapes and rejects empty segments; upstream does a plain split('.')
config.rustEvidence: app-server/src/config_manager_service.rs:402-410 parse_key_path: rejects only empty/whitespace input, otherwise `path.split('.').map(ToString::to_string).collect()` — quotes and backslashes are literal characters, and `a..b` yields ["a","","b"] (no rejection of empty segments).
config.swiftStatus: RequestRouter.swift:6629-6664 parseConfigKeyPath implements a quote/escape mini-parser: a leading double-quote opens a quoted segment, backslash escapes inside quotes, and empty segments throw "keyPath segments must not be empty".
config.description: For a keyPath containing quotes/backslashes or empty segments, Swift and upstream produce different segment lists (or Swift errors where upstream succeeds). E.g. keyPath '"a.b"' becomes ["a.b"] in Swift but ["\"a","b\""] upstream; 'a..b' is accepted upstream as ["a","","b"] but rejected by Swift. Affects only key names with dots/quotes — uncommon — but is a real parse-semantics divergence on a wire-facing parameter.
config.fixRecommendation: Replace parseConfigKeyPath with a plain split on '.' (rejecting only fully-empty/whitespace input) to match upstream parse_key_path exactly, or document the intentional superset. Keeping upstream's exact behavior is safest for round-trip fidelity.

config.title: Project-layer version fingerprint hashed over raw pre-sanitize file rather than sanitized+alias-normalized config
config.rustEvidence: config/src/loader/mod.rs:1203-1225 builds the project ConfigLayerEntry from `config` AFTER sanitize_project_config (denylist removal), resolve_relative_paths_in_config_toml, and merge_root_checkout_project_hooks; ConfigLayerEntry::new computes version via version_for_toml over that sanitized config (state.rs:107-117, fingerprint.rs:37-49). So a project layer's reported version reflects the post-denylist/normalized table.
config.swiftStatus: RequestRouter.swift:6336-6348 rawLayerVersion for a .project layer re-reads `<dot>/config.toml` RAW via readUserConfigTOML and hashes it (ConfigCanonicalVersion.version), i.e. INCLUDING any denylisted keys and without alias normalization. This version is what config/read layers[] reports for project layers (RequestRouter.swift:1975).
config.description: The version string Swift reports for a project layer in config/read differs from upstream whenever the project config.toml contains denylisted keys (openai_base_url, model_provider, etc.) or [memories] legacy aliases, since upstream hashes the sanitized table and Swift hashes the raw file. app-server-registry.swiftStatus: Sources/Supervisor/RequestRouter.swift is a single `public actor` (line 37) that serializes request ENTRY but yields at every `await`, so two in-flight same-scope requests (e.g. concurrent `config/value/write`, or two `turn/start` on the same thread) can interleave at await points. No equivalent of `RequestSerializationQueueKey`/serialization scopes exists anywhere in Sources/. Config writes are partially protected by an `expectedVersion` optimistic-concurrency check (RequestRouter.swift:1973, 6121-6168).
app-server-registry.description: Upstream guarantees same-scope serialization and explicit concurrency for `serialization: None` methods; the Swift actor model provides neither precise guarantee. In practice the version-check on config writes and the actor entry-serialization mitigate corruption, but observable ordering of concurrent same-thread/same-resource requests can differ from upstream, and there is no protection for scopes lacking an internal version check (e.g. `global("account-auth")`, `global("mcp-registry")`, `global("windows-sandbox-setup")`).
app-server-registry.fixRecommendation: If strict parity is required, add a per-connection serialization-queue keyed by an analogue of `ClientRequestSerializationScope` (thread_id / global(name) / command_process_id / fs_watch_id / fuzzy_session_id) in RequestRouter so same-scope handlers await each other while None-scope methods stay concurrent. Otherwise document this as an accepted divergence (the actor + version-check defense is adequate for the corruption-prevention goal).

app-server-registry.title: Per-connection RPC gate (ConnectionRpcGate shutdown) has no Swift equivalent
app-server-registry.rustEvidence: app-server/src/connection_rpc_gate.rs:11-48 defines `ConnectionRpcGate` with `shutdown()` that flips `accepting=false`, closes the TaskTracker, and awaits in-flight handlers; message_processor.rs:706 calls `session_state.rpc_gate.shutdown()` in `connection_closed` so queued-but-not-started initialized handlers are dropped while started ones finish before connection teardown completes.
app-server-registry.swiftStatus: RequestRouter.connectionClosed (Sources/Supervisor/RequestRouter.swift:819-835) tears down file/skills watchers, login flows, fuzzy/command/process sessions, but there is no gate that prevents already-queued initialized handlers from starting after close, nor an await for in-flight handlers to drain. grep for `RpcGate`/`rpc_gate`/`accepting` in Sources/Supervisor returns nothing.
app-server-registry.description: On connection close, upstream drops not-yet-started handlers and waits for started ones; the Swift port relies on the actor finishing its current continuation and on per-feature cleanup. A handler that started before close can still emit a response/notification to a torn-down connection (send becomes a no-op) and there is no explicit barrier. This is largely benign because `conn.send` to a closed connection is a no-op, so it does not produce wire-visible garbage to other clients.
app-server-registry.fixRecommendation: Optional: introduce a lightweight per-connection accepting-flag checked at the top of dispatch plus a drain/await of in-flight request Tasks in connectionClosed, mirroring ConnectionRpcGate. Low priority given the no-op send semantics; acceptable to document as a divergence.

session-turn-loop.title: Mailbox accept/defer delivery semantics not wired into the turn loop
session-turn-loop.rustEvidence: core/src/stream_events_utils.rs:353-364 — on a tool call `sess.accept_mailbox_delivery_for_current_turn(&sub_id)`; record_completed_response_item_with_finalized_facts (lines 160-163) calls `sess.defer_mailbox_delivery_to_next_turn(&sub_id)` when `defers_mailbox_delivery` (a final-answer assistant message that is NOT MessagePhase::Commentary, or an ImageGenerationCall). completed_item_defers_mailbox_delivery_to_next_turn (lines 558-574) drives the gate.
session-turn-loop.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/Mailbox.swift faithfully ports the InterAgentCommunication struct and the Mailbox queue (send/drain/hasPendingTriggerTurn), but a grep of SessionEngine.swift for accept_mailbox/defer_mailbox/MessagePhase/commentary returns no matches — the engine never calls an accept-on-tool-call or defer-on-final-answer step. Mailbox is consumed only via trigger-turn draining at turn start.
session-turn-loop.description: Upstream decides per-completed-item whether queued inter-agent mail is delivered within the current turn (deferred until after a final answer) vs immediately. The Swift turn loop has no equivalent accept/defer step, so mail delivery is not phase-gated. This only affects the multi-agent mailbox flow, which the Swift port implements as a simplified internal subsystem (AgentOrchestrator in MultiAgent.swift) rather than the full upstream agent/ thread-spawn machinery; for a single-session frontend there is no wire-visible effect.
session-turn-loop.fixRecommendation: If multi-agent mailbox fidelity is required, add accept/defer hooks in SessionEngine's output-item handling: on a tool-call completed item, accept current-turn delivery; on a non-commentary final-answer assistant message (or image-generation call), defer pending mailbox items to the next turn. Otherwise document as an intentional simplification.

session-turn-loop.title: Mid-turn budget-limit goal steering item is not injected

exec-unified-shell.title: Remote unified_exec uses login shell (-lc) for free-form command strings, diverging from the security-hardened local -c path
exec-unified-shell.rustEvidence: core/src/tools/handlers/unified_exec.rs:97-122 get_command: Direct mode derives argv via shell.derive_exec_args(&args.cmd, use_login_shell); shell.rs:43-52 uses "-lc" only when use_login_shell is true, and unified_exec login defaults to allow_login_shell (false by default), so the standard path is "-c" (no login init files).
exec-unified-shell.swiftStatus: Sources/Tools/RemoteExecServerTools.swift:666-672 RemoteExecServerUnifiedExecTool.CommandSpec.line returns ["/bin/sh","-lc",line] unconditionally — hardcoded login shell and hardcoded /bin/sh (not the user's default shell). The local UnifiedExec.swift:711-725 deliberately uses -c to avoid sourcing ~/.zshenv as a secret side-channel; the remote tool does the opposite.
exec-unified-shell.description: The remote unified_exec free-form-string path always runs `/bin/sh -lc`, which (a) sources the remote user's login init files and (b) ignores the user's configured shell. Upstream's default is `-c` on the resolved user shell, not `-lc` on /bin/sh. Behavioral and (on the remote side) a re-introduction of the login-init side-channel the local port explicitly removed.
exec-unified-shell.fixRecommendation: In Sources/Tools/RemoteExecServerTools.swift RemoteExecServerUnifiedExecTool.CommandSpec.line, change ["/bin/sh","-lc",line] to a non-login form (["/bin/sh","-c",line]) for parity with the local UnifiedExec/ShellTool default, matching upstream get_command's allow_login_shell=false default.

exec-unified-shell.title: exec_command/write_stdin render mutually-exclusive exit_code vs session_id, but upstream emits both when an alive process already has an exit code
exec-unified-shell.rustEvidence: core/src/tools/context.rs:410-416 response_text(): emits "Process exited with code {exit_code}" whenever self.exit_code.is_some() AND separately "Process running with session ID {process_id}" whenever self.process_id.is_some(); these are independent. process_manager.rs:509-516 ProcessStatus::Alive carries Some(process_id) together with a possibly-Some exit_code, so both lines can appear in one response.
exec-unified-shell.swiftStatus: Sources/Tools/UnifiedExec.swift:953-958 renderExecJSON gates them mutually-exclusively: `if exited, let code` emits exit line; `if !exited, let sid` emits session line. A still-alive process that already has a recorded exit_code would print neither the exit line nor (since exit_code is set) match upstream's both-lines output.
exec-unified-shell.description: In the (rare) state where a unified-exec process is still tracked alive but exit_code() already returns Some, upstream prints both the 'Process exited with code N' and 'Process running with session ID M' sections; the Swift renderer prints only the session line and never the exit-code line for an alive process. Output-text divergence in an edge case.
exec-unified-shell.fixRecommendation: In renderExecJSON, decouple the two conditions to match context.rs: emit the exit-code line whenever exitCode != nil (not gated on exited), and emit the session-id line whenever sessionId != nil for a non-exited process, allowing both to appear together.

exec-unified-shell.title: exec_command `shell` parameter does not derive correct argv for non-POSIX shells (PowerShell/Cmd)
exec-unified-shell.rustEvidence: core/src/shell.rs:43-70 derive_exec_args: PowerShell uses [path, ("-NoProfile" unless login), "-Command", command]; Cmd uses [path, "/c", command]; only Zsh/Bash/Sh use -c/-lc. unified_exec.rs:108-117 builds the model-provided shell via get_shell_by_model_provided_path then derive_exec_args, honoring per-shell-type arg conventions.
exec-unified-shell.swiftStatus: Sources/Tools/UnifiedExec.swift:1054-1064 CmdSpec.argv(shell:useLoginShell:) always produces [sh, useLoginShell ? "-lc" : "-c", s] regardless of the shell binary. A model passing shell:"pwsh" or shell:"cmd" gets `pwsh -c <script>` / `cmd -c <script>` instead of `-Command` / `/c`.
exec-unified-shell.description: When the model supplies a non-POSIX `shell` (PowerShell/Cmd), the Swift exec_command builds POSIX `-c` argv that the target shell will not interpret correctly. Upstream detects the shell type and uses the proper invocation flags. Low impact on macOS where POSIX shells dominate.
exec-unified-shell.fixRecommendation: In UnifiedExec.swift CmdSpec.argv, detect the shell binary basename (pwsh/powershell → ["-Command"], cmd → ["/c"], else -c/-lc) mirroring shell.rs::derive_exec_args, instead of unconditionally using -c/-lc.

exec-unified-shell.title: Remote process/write response WriteStatus (stdinClosed/unknownProcess/starting) is ignored
exec-unified-shell.rustEvidence: exec-server/src/protocol.rs:133-146 WriteStatus enum (camelCase: accepted/unknownProcess/stdinClosed/starting) and WriteResponse{status}; a write to a closed-stdin or unknown process returns a non-Accepted status rather than an error.

apply-patch.title: Fuzzy seek_sequence rstrip/trim passes use ASCII-only whitespace, not Rust's Unicode White_Space — exotic trailing whitespace fails to match
apply-patch.rustEvidence: apply-patch/src/seek_sequence.rs:44 `lines[i + p_idx].trim_end() != pat.trim_end()` and :57 `lines[i + p_idx].trim() != pat.trim()`. Rust `str::trim_end`/`trim` strip by `char::is_whitespace()` (Unicode White_Space), which includes U+0085 (NEL), U+1680, U+2000, U+2001, U+2028, U+2029 — code points NOT covered by the later normalise() pass (seek_sequence.rs:88-90 only maps U+00A0, U+2002-200A, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000 to space).
apply-patch.swiftStatus: Sources/Tools/ApplyPatch.swift:687-706 — `asciiWhitespace` is restricted to U+20, U+09, U+0A, U+0D, U+0B, U+0C; `trimEnd`/`fullTrim` use only that set. The header comment (lines 678-686) asserts "the only White_Space scalars that can appear ... are ASCII," which is incorrect: a patch context line or file line may contain a trailing U+2028/U+0085/U+1680/U+2000/U+2001. For those, Rust's rstrip/trim passes match but Swift's do not, and Swift's normalise() (lines 708-729) also does not map them to space, so the match fails entirely → contextMismatch where upstream applies cleanly.
apply-patch.description: Upstream fuzzy matching tolerates trailing/leading Unicode whitespace (full White_Space set) at the rstrip and trim stages; the Swift port only tolerates ASCII whitespace. Lines whose only difference is an exotic Unicode whitespace char (NEL, line/paragraph separator, Ogham space, en/em quad) will fail to match in Swift but succeed in Rust, producing a spurious "Failed to find expected lines" / "Failed to find context" error.
apply-patch.fixRecommendation: In Sources/Tools/ApplyPatch.swift, broaden `asciiWhitespace` (used by `trimEnd`/`fullTrim`) to the full Unicode White_Space set Rust uses — add U+0085, U+1680, U+2000-200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000, U+00A0 — OR implement trimEnd/fullTrim via a predicate matching `Unicode.Scalar.properties.isWhitespace`. Update the now-inaccurate comment at lines 678-686.

apply-patch.title: In-hunk header detection breaks on indented (leading-whitespace) hunk markers where upstream treats them as context lines
apply-patch.rustEvidence: apply-patch/src/parser.rs:334 `if remaining_lines[0].starts_with('*') { break; }` — the next-hunk check tests the RAW (untrimmed) line for a literal leading `*`. An indented line like `"  *** Add File: x"` does NOT start with `*`, so it is passed to parse_update_file_chunk and consumed as a context line (its first char is space → old/new line `" *** Add File: x"`).
apply-patch.swiftStatus: Sources/Tools/ApplyPatch.swift:533-534 `if raw.hasPrefix("*") || raw.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).hasPrefix("*** ") { break }` — the extra trimmed `"*** "` test causes Swift to break out of the update body on an indented `*** ...` line that upstream would instead absorb as hunk content.
apply-patch.description: For an update hunk body containing a line that begins with whitespace followed by `*** `, upstream consumes it as a context line whereas Swift terminates the current hunk and re-parses it as a new hunk header (likely yielding a different parse result or an 'is not a valid hunk header' error). Affects only malformed/edge-case patches but is an observable parse-divergence.
apply-patch.fixRecommendation: In Sources/Tools/ApplyPatch.swift:533-534, drop the `|| raw.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).hasPrefix("*** ")` clause and break only on a raw leading `*` (`raw.hasPrefix("*")`) to match upstream parser.rs:334 exactly.

persistence-rollout.title: Rollout session_meta records source="mcp" instead of the app-server default "vscode"

persistence-rollout.title: SessionMeta omits always-serialized null fields base_instructions and model_provider when nil
